key_insight: EVATok adaptively assigns variable numbers of discrete tokens to different temporal blocks of a video based on their visual complexity, cutting wasted tokens on static/repetitive segments while preserving detail where needed to make autoregressive video generation more efficient.
problem_solved: Fixed-length tokenization treats all video segments equally, wasting representation capacity on simple frames and inflating autoregressive computation; EVATok addresses the trade-off between reconstruction quality and generation cost by allocating tokens adaptively across time.
method: Learn a per-block token allocation policy that predicts how many discrete tokens each temporal block needs based on motion/complexity indicators.
Compress video frames into variable-length discrete token sequences under a global token budget, enabling higher fidelity for complex regions and fewer tokens for simple/repetitive parts.
Plug the adaptive token sequences into standard visual autoregressive generators to reduce sequence length (and hence compute) while maintaining reconstruction and generation quality.
impact: By reducing unnecessary tokens and shortening autoregressive sequences, EVATok lowers compute, memory and latency for video generation, enabling higher-resolution or longer-duration outputs and faster training/inference for practitioners.

paper_title: EVATok: Adaptive Length Video Tokenization for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Tianwei Xiong, Jun Hao Liew, Zilong Huang, Zhijie Lin, Jiashi Feng
